concepts.name: Agamas: Structure, Canonicity, and Sectarian Disputes
key_dimensions: The 12 Angas as the primary canonical texts and their content overview
Digambara vs Shvetambara dispute: Digambaras reject the authenticity of surviving Agamas while Shvetambaras accept them
The lost 12th Anga (Drishtivada) and its significance in the canon
Council of Vallabhi (5th–6th century CE) and its role in finalizing Shvetambara canon

concepts.name: The 12 Angas: Content and Hierarchical Importance
key_dimensions: Acharanga Sutra as the oldest Anga containing rules of conduct for monks and information about Mahavira's life
Sutrakritanga dealing with refutation of other philosophical doctrines
Bhagavati Sutra (Vyakhyaprajnapti) as the largest Anga covering cosmology, geography, and dialogues of Mahavira
UPSC trap: distinguishing which Anga is oldest vs which is largest vs which deals with specific themes

concepts.name: Upangas, Chedasutras, and Mulasutras: Sub-canonical Literature
key_dimensions: 12 Upangas as subsidiary texts supplementing the Angas with cosmological and narrative content
Chedasutras (6 texts) dealing specifically with monastic discipline and rules of expiation
Mulasutras as foundational texts for novice monks, including Uttaradhyayana Sutra
UPSC trap: Uttaradhyayana Sutra classified under Mulasutras, not Angas, yet contains key philosophical teachings

concepts.name: Acharanga Sutra: Historical and Literary Significance
key_dimensions: Oldest surviving Jain text and one of the oldest texts in Prakrit literature
Primary source for Mahavira's biography, austerities, and enlightenment narrative
Contains rules of conduct (Yama) for Jain monks including the five great vows (Mahavratas)
Language: Ardhamagadhi Prakrit — its significance for understanding early Middle Indo-Aryan languages

concepts.name: Ardhamagadhi Prakrit: Language of Jain Canonical Literature
key_dimensions: Considered the language spoken by Mahavira and the sacred language of Shvetambara canon
Distinction from Pali (language of Buddhist canon) and Sanskrit — UPSC often tests this comparison
Role of Ardhamagadhi in the development of regional languages like Gujarati and Rajasthani
Digambara texts written in Shauraseni Prakrit — key sectarian linguistic divide

concepts.name: Digambara Literary Tradition: Shatkhandagama and Kasayapahuda
key_dimensions: Shatkhandagama ('Scripture in Six Parts') as the most sacred Digambara canonical text
Composed by Pushpadanta and Bhutabali in early centuries CE — regarded as partial preservation of lost Drishtivada
Kasayapahuda dealing with the doctrine of passions (kasayas) and their role in karmic bondage
UPSC trap: These are Digambara equivalents of canonical texts, not accepted by Shvetambaras

concepts.name: Tattvartha Sutra by Umasvati: The Universal Jain Text
key_dimensions: Only philosophical text accepted by BOTH Digambara and Shvetambara sects — unique in Jain literature
Systematizes Jain metaphysics: nine tattvas (realities), doctrine of karma, soul, and liberation
Written in Sanskrit, marking a shift from Prakrit — significance for Jain intellectual history
Comparable in function to Brahmasutra for Vedanta — UPSC may ask about cross-tradition comparisons

concepts.name: Jain Councils and Canonization of Literature
key_dimensions: First Jain Council at Pataliputra (3rd century BCE) under Sthulabhadra — early attempt at canon compilation
Second Jain Council (Council of Vallabhi, ~5th century CE) under Devardhigani — final Shvetambara canon
Digambara rejection of both councils' outcomes as basis for their claim that original texts are lost
UPSC trap: Comparison with Buddhist Councils — different outcomes, different languages, different locations

concepts.name: Uttaradhyayana Sutra: Philosophical and Narrative Content
key_dimensions: 36 chapters containing dialogues, parables, and philosophical discourses attributed to Mahavira
Contains the famous dialogue between Mahavira and Gosala (founder of Ajivikas) — source for understanding rival sects
Covers Jain ethics, concept of the soul, karma theory, and path to liberation
UPSC relevance: Primary source for understanding Jainism's relationship with contemporaneous heterodox sects

concepts.name: Jain Narrative Literature: Kathakosh and Parishishtaparvan
key_dimensions: Parishishtaparvan by Hemachandra (12th century CE): biographical accounts of Mahavira's disciples — key historical source
Kathakosh tradition: collections of didactic stories used for moral instruction, parallel to Buddhist Jataka tales
UPSC trap: Parishishtaparvan is a primary source for Chandragupta Maurya's alleged Jain conversion — historically significant
Narrative literature as a vehicle for propagating Jain ethics beyond monastic audiences

concepts.name: Hemachandra and Medieval Jain Sanskrit Literature
key_dimensions: 12th century Shvetambara scholar-monk: polymath who wrote on grammar, poetry, logic, and biography
Trishashthishalaka-purusha-charitra: lives of 63 illustrious beings — encyclopedic Jain universal history
Yogashastra: treatise on Jain yoga and ethics — shows Jain engagement with Yoga traditions
Patronage of Chalukya king Kumarapala — example of royal patronage shaping literary production; UPSC PYQ connection

concepts.name: Jain Logic and Epistemological Literature: Anekantavada in Texts
key_dimensions: Syadvada (doctrine of conditional predication) and Nayavada (doctrine of viewpoints) as Jain epistemological contributions
Saptabhangi (seven-fold predication) systematized in texts like Anuyogadvara Sutra
Akalanka and Vidyanandi as key Jain logicians whose texts engaged with Buddhist and Brahmanical logic
UPSC relevance: Anekantavada as a philosophical concept — tested in both Prelims (identification) and Mains (comparative philosophy)

concepts.name: Jain Literature as Historical Source: Political and Social History
key_dimensions: Bhagavati Sutra mentions 16 Mahajanapadas and contemporaneous rulers — cross-verification with Buddhist sources
Acharanga Sutra provides geographical information about regions where Mahavira preached
Parishishtaparvan's account of Chandragupta Maurya: corroboration and limitations as historical evidence
UPSC trap: Jain texts as sources for Mauryan history — what they confirm vs what remains contested

concepts.name: Jain Literature in Regional Languages: Kannada and Tamil Contributions
key_dimensions: Jainism's major role in early Kannada literature: Adipurana by Pampa, Shantipurana — Jain authors dominant in 9th–10th century CE
Thirukkural by Thiruvalluvar: debated Jain influence — UPSC frequently tests this contested attribution
Silappatikaram and Manimekalai: Jain and Buddhist themes in Sangam-era epics respectively
UPSC trap: distinguishing Jain vs Buddhist contributions to early regional literature

concepts.name: Kalpasutra by Bhadrabahu: Biography of Tirthankaras and Monastic Rules
key_dimensions: Contains biographies of the last four Tirthankaras, especially Mahavira — primary hagiographic source
Section on Parshvanatha: evidence for pre-Mahavira Jain tradition and the four-vow system vs Mahavira's five vows
Samachari section lays down rules for monastic conduct during Paryushana festival
UPSC trap: Bhadrabahu is associated with both Kalpasutra AND the alleged southward migration of Jains to Karnataka — same person, different contexts

concepts.name: Jain Cosmological Literature: Lokavibhaga and Trilokasara
key_dimensions: Lokavibhaga: earliest known Indian text to use the decimal place-value number system — significant for history of mathematics
Trilokasara by Nemichandra: systematic account of Jain cosmology including universe structure (loka)
Jain cosmological texts as sources for understanding ancient Indian scientific thought
UPSC relevance: Lokavibhaga's mathematical significance — often cited in questions on history of Indian mathematics

concepts.name: Comparison of Jain and Buddhist Literary Canons: Key Distinctions
key_dimensions: Language: Ardhamagadhi (Jain Shvetambara) vs Pali (Theravada Buddhist) vs Sanskrit (both traditions later)
Canonization: Jain councils more contested and later than Buddhist councils; Digambara rejection has no Buddhist parallel
Content focus: Jain canon more focused on cosmology and karma mechanics; Buddhist Tripitaka has Vinaya-Sutta-Abhidhamma tripartite structure
UPSC trap: Both traditions have 'Agamas' — Buddhist Agamas (in Pali/Sanskrit) are different from Jain Agamas; same term, different corpus

concepts.name: Doctrine of Karma in Jain Literature: Textual Basis and Uniqueness
key_dimensions: Kasayapahuda and Shatkhandagama as primary Digambara sources for karma theory
Jain karma as a physical substance (pudgala) — distinct from Buddhist and Hindu karma concepts — tested in comparative philosophy questions
Eight types of karma (Ghatiya and Aghatiya) systematized in canonical and post-canonical texts
UPSC trap: Jain karma theory is more mechanistic and material than Buddhist karma — a key philosophical distinction

concepts.name: Jain Poetics and Grammatical Literature: Apabhramsha Contributions
key_dimensions: Hemachandra's Apabhramsha grammar (Deshivibhasha): foundational source for understanding transition to modern NW Indian languages
Jain poets' role in developing Apabhramsha as a literary medium — precursor to Old Gujarati and Rajasthani
Sandesha Rasaka and other Apabhramsha works: Jain literary aesthetics and narrative traditions
UPSC relevance: Jain contribution to Indian linguistic history — connects Ancient History to Art & Culture syllabus
